source_document.note: Built from the finalized, corrected PDF. Every text line of the PDF is present in `document` (verbatim, with light markdown). Hyperlinks, tables and image transcriptions are included.

verification.statement: Every OUAC code and every date/timeline in the PDF was checked against live official pages (OUInfo, OUAC, or the university). Other official details were spot-checked where noted. Pages can change after these dates.

prepared.statement: Structural only. No date, grade, course code, source or claim was added, removed or altered. See prepare-changelog.json for every change.

claim_types.official: Stated by an official source (university, OUAC or OUInfo) or a faithful summary of one.
claim_types.editorial: Analysis, comparison or advice written by the document's authors, based on the sources — not a quote from a university.
claim_types.third_party: Admissions consultancies, guides, data aggregators (e.g. Youthfully, AdmissionPrep, GrantMe, MYLS, Uniscope, ScholarTree, AdmissionsAlly). Not official.
claim_types.community: Applicant reports: Reddit, screenshots of applicant posts, unattributed slides, and claims written into the document with no named source. Not official; treat as anecdotal.
claim_types.secondary_press: News or student press (The Queen's Journal, The Varsity).
claim_types.vendor: The assessment vendor (Kira Talent) — not the university.
claim_types.internal_note: Notes addressed to the website team (publishing advice, open questions, checklists). Not intended for students as-is.
claim_types.source_list: Source lists printed in the document.
claim_types.verification_note: Notes added during verification (check dates, corrections, stale-page notes).
claim_types.mixed: The block combines more than one claim type; see `contains`.

verification_statuses.certified: Matches a live official page opened 15–17 September 2026 (verbatim evidence in `verification`).
verification_statuses.contradiction: Official sources disagree; both versions are kept and linked to a record in `contradictions`.
verification_statuses.unconfirmed: Kept as written but not found on any official page checked; marked in the PDF (blue highlight).
verification_statuses.not_yet_published: The university has not published it for 2027 yet; expected timing given.
verification_statuses.not_individually_verified: Taken from the document and attributed to the sources it cites, but not individually re-opened in the verification pass.
verification_statuses.community_unverified: Community or third-party figure; not verifiable against an official source.

source_attribution.block: Sources named or linked for this exact block.
source_attribution.section: Block inherits the sources the document cites for its section.
source_attribution.none: No source applies (editorial, internal, or unsourced community text).

contradiction_types.official_stale_page: An official page still shows an earlier cycle or old detail.
contradiction_types.official_internal: One official page disagrees with itself.
contradiction_types.secondary_vs_official: Press/consultancy account differs from the official one.
contradiction_types.official_vs_community: Community or third-party figures differ from official ones.
contradiction_types.community_disagreement: Community/third-party sources disagree with each other.
contradiction_types.document_internal: The document itself says two incompatible things.

how_to_use: programs[] holds the structured, website-ready facts for each program. Each fact has claim_type, verification.status, sources, contradiction_ids and pdf_block_ids.
supplementary_applications[] summarises each supplementary component; the full guide text is in document (use content_section_id).
document.parts[].sections[].blocks[] is the complete PDF content in reading order, each block tagged with claim_type and sources.
contradictions[] lists every place sources (or the document) disagree, with each side quoted and sourced.
sources{} is keyed by source id; ids starting S_ are official pages, T_ third-party, C_ community, V_ vendor, P_ press.
Dates are ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD); date_text keeps the wording shown in the document. Fields with in_pdf=false were recorded during verification but are not printed in the PDF.

contradictions[].statements[].pdf_block_ids are where each side is printed; guidance_block_ids hold the document's advice about it; related_block_ids are other places in the document that repeat one side. Every one of those blocks carries the contradiction id in its own contradiction_ids.

Tables (comparisons[] and document table blocks) carry cell_annotations: per-cell claim_type, sources, verification_status and contradiction_ids for cells that need them; any cell not listed takes default_cell_claim_type.

For a fact with verification.status "unconfirmed", `sources` are the pages the document cites and that were checked; they do NOT state the unconfirmed detail (see verification.note and the log rows in verification.log_ids).

contradiction_ids on any fact point to records in contradictions[] where some source (official, third-party, community, or the document itself) says something different about that item. The fact's verification.status still describes the fact as stated: "certified" means it matches a live official page; "contradiction" means official sources disagree on that exact value and both versions are kept.

deadline_kinds.deadline: A real application/submission deadline. Only these belong in countdowns and urgency states.
deadline_kinds.opens: A date something opens, not a deadline.
deadline_kinds.decision_window: A range in which offers are released. Usually has no single date.
deadline_kinds.milestone: An administrative date, not an applicant action.
deadline_kinds.ongoing: A continuing obligation with no single date.
deadline_kinds.prior_cycle: A date from a PREVIOUS admission cycle. Never present as upcoming.
deadline_kinds.none: Explicitly records that no such deadline exists.

derived_fields.note: Computed from this file by the preparation pass. Not source data. Regenerate if any source value changes.
derived_fields.programs[].deadlines[].is_deadline: kind === "deadline" AND date is a parseable ISO date. The only rows safe for date math.
derived_fields.programs[].deadlines[].date_range: {start,end} when the source gave a range instead of a single date; date is null in that case.
derived_fields.programs[].supp_app_required: True only if a linked supplementary_applications record has required === true.
derived_fields.programs[].inherited_from: Map of field -> program_id this program inherits that field from.
derived_fields.*.requirement_level: "required" | "recommended" | null, normalized from the original free-text requirement (which is preserved).
derived_fields.*.evaluable: False when the entry is a prose constraint rather than a course code. The checker must not pass or fail these.
derived_fields.supplementary_applications[].traps: Author analysis extracted from the corrected source document. claim_type is always "editorial" — these are NOT university statements and must be visibly labelled as analysis on the site.
derived_fields.supplementary_applications[].weighting: McMaster BHSc only. claim_type "official" because McMaster presented it; verification "unconfirmed" because it exists only as an open house slide observed first-hand, with no published URL. Must render with that caveat visible.
